[Section I - Preamble, Definitions]
ABOUT UNIVERSITY
Vidyashilp University is the culmination of an outstanding legacy of the Vidyashilp
Education Group, committed to excellence in education. Vidyashilp University aims to
foster an environment and culture of collaboration, responsiveness, high performance and
service. We are people-centred and have a strongly desire to provide a unique Vidyashilp
Experience to our students and staff, focused on nurturing students who will become self-
aware, confident, empathetic and resourceful leaders who will serve society to the best of
their abilities.
The VU Experience fosters a climate for collaboration between individuals and groups from
diverse cultures and backgrounds. VU creates a diverse, inclusive community and
environment where VU faculty, staff, students and parents, and alumni feel connected to
one another by a common sense of purpose, pride, and spirit, and develop a distinctive
ability to work, learn, lead and serve in diverse contexts.
section: Section I - Preamble, Definitions, p. 1

text:
[Section I - Preamble, Definitions]
VU’s primary educational goal is the cultivation of deep domain knowledge within each
student’s chosen field. We believe that investing in all domains of our differentiated focus
areas is essential to create intellectual capital to drive progress and achieve excellence. At
VU, our schools don’t function in silos but rather with an interdisciplinary dependence.
We focus on a problem -solving approach and provide program choices across all four
schools with a curriculum established in Data Science, Digital Business, Design Studies,
Legal Studies and Liberal Arts.
VISION, MISSION AND CORE VALUES
OUR VISION
We aspire to provide meaningful, collective learning experiences that result in
conscientious leadership for a progressive, yet sustainable society.
OUR MISSION
x We inspire people locally, nationally and globally by extending access to Vidyashilp
University’s innovative teaching and resources through inclusive and flexible
opportunities to study and research.
section: Section I - Preamble, Definitions, p. 1

text:
[Section I - Preamble, Definitions]
x To develop human values and human potential to its fullest extent so that
intellectually capable and imaginatively gifted leaders can emerge in a range of
professions.
OUR VALUES
INTEGRITY – We embrace integrity as a central value in all aspects of personal and
professional engagement – including learning, teaching, governance and service – to instil
a culture of trust and accountability.
ACADEMIC FREEDOM – We affirm the principles of academic freedom for both students
and teachers, their rights and responsibilities to advance knowledge through research and
creativity, and to educate students to develop their own independence of mind.
DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION – We assert that diversity and interplay of
differences is essential to educational excellence and to enrich the individual and collective
learning experiences.
Short Title, Commencement and Application
a. These Regulations shall be called Academic Regulations.

[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]
1 ADMISSION
Admission to the Universityshall be open to all persons irrespective of caste, class,
creed, gender, abilities, or nationality. All admissions shall be made on the basis
of merit in the qualifying examinations and as per the rules and guidelines
prescribed by the Government of Karnataka, other concerned regulatory bodies
and the entrance examinations conducted by the University.
The students shall be admitted to a Program subject to fulfilment of eligibility
criteria, as prescribed by the University for the respective Program.
A student admitted to a Program of study, shall continue to remain registered for
such a Program, till they successfully complete the Program or withdraw from the
Program in accordance with the concerned Program Regulations.
Every student duly admitted to the University for a Program after compliance with
prescribed formalities and payment of prescribed fees as applicable and other
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy, p. 7

text:
[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]
amounts and submission of prescribed documents and certificates shall be allotted
a University Enrolment Number OR UEN.
If a student fails to pay the University Fee, or fails to produce all the mandatory
documents and certificates required for admission to the University before the
prescribed last date, the Provisional Offer of Admission to the student shall stand
withdrawn.
If a student desires to join the University on the basis of Lateral Entry or Transfer
of Credits from other Institutes/Universities during the Program, they shall be
examined for eligibility for admission as per the procedure and criteria laid down
in the Academic Regulations of the University and the concerned Program
Regulations, and admission shall be dependent on their eligibility so determined.
Confirmation of admission and enrolment in the University is subject to fulfilment
of the eligibility criteria.
2 FEE POLICY
a. The University fee consists of components such as Tuition Fee, Security Deposit
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy, p. 7

text:
[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]
(Refundable), Examination Fee, Convocation Fee and such other components as may
be prescribed by the Board of Management from time to time.
b. Every program of the University has a prescribed University Fee. Further the Fee
Structure and the payment schedule for the entire duration of the concerned program
is announced by way of notification before the commencement of each academic year.
c. The Tuition Fee always means the Annual Tuition Fee for an academic year for a
program. The Annual Tuition Fee does not include the expenses / charges for extra-
curricular activities, local / international educational trips and other value-added
programs that may be introduced from time to time.
d. The Security Deposit is a Refundable Security Deposit without any interest, subject
to deduction of outstanding dues if any, after the student graduates from the program
or discontinues from the program or for whatever the reason(s).
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy, pp. 7-8

text:

e. The Payment Schedule of the University Fee must be strictly adhered to, by all the
students. Failure to comply shall result in the student not being eligible for
registration to the concerned academic year and late fee will be charged accordingly.
Further, the students are cautioned that this could lead to the loss of an academic
year.
f. Vidyashilp University shall not be obliged to send any reminders for payment of the
University Fee. If it is done, it is only in the interest of students and cannot be
demanded or referred to in the event of failure to pay the University Fee as per the
specified schedule.
g. The University Fee Structure is subject to change from time to time and shall be
notified by the University. The University’s decision regarding changes in fee structure
is final and binding on all concerned.

a. All fee payments should necessarily be made online only using the login credentials

b. The Fee is payable in INR only

f. The University shall not be responsible for any fee amount returned to the payer

[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]
The policies relating to the University Fee and Deposits, where applicable, are the

5 FEE CONCESSION AND SCHOLARSHIP POLICY
Introduction:
Vidyashilp University is committed for providing the best education opportunities to
motivated students. The University has established various categories of scholarships to
encourage and enable students to pursue education at Vidyashilp University.
Scholarships are provided to reward and support meritorious and talented students, who
have demonstrated exceptional performance in academics, sports and co-curricular
activities. The University is particularly committed to enabling meritorious students with
financial constraints, differently abled students and achievers at the state and national
levels, through appropriate scholarships.
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy, pp. 9-10

text:
[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]
5.1 Categories of Scholarships
To cater to the different needs and circumstances of meritorious students, the University
offers four (04) categories of Scholarships.
5.1.1 Merit-based Scholarship at the time of Admission
Merit scholarships are awarded to students with outstanding academic
performance. This scholarship is awarded at the time of admission to the 1 st year
of a program.
Two (02) sub-categories of Merit Scholarships are offered:
5.1.2 Outstanding achievement in State / National / International Level Entrance
Examinations:
This Scholarship is awarded based on the performance in the State / National /
International Level Entrance Examinations specified for a particular program.
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy (5.1), p. 10

text:
[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]
5.1.3 Meritorious Performance in the Qualifying Examination:
The Scholarship is awarded based on the performance in the Qualifying
Examinations (State / National / International Boards). The details of the extent
of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are as per the scholarship
policy and subject to approval by the Scholarship Committee.
5.2 Enabling Scholarship
The University is committed to ensure that a meritorious student is not hindered
from pursuing education at Vidyashilp due to financial constraints.
Three (03) sub-categories of enabling scholarships are offered:
5.2.1 Low Income Based Scholarship
This scholarship is offered to enable meritorious students whose family income is
a constraint to meet the tuition fees of the program.
5.2.2 Single Parent (Mother) Income Based Scholarship.
This Scholarship is specifically offered to a student with Single Parent (Mother)
having financial constraints to pursue education at Vidyashilp.
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy (5.1.3), pp. 10-11

text:
[Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy]

This scholarship is offered to a meritorious student whose parent (father/mother)

5.2.4 The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are

This scholarship is awarded to recognize and encourage students who have excelled in

State/ National / International levels.
The University is also committed to encourage differently -abled students to pursue
education at Vidyashilp University.
Two (02) sub-categories of Encouragement Scholarships are offered:
section: Section II - Admission Rules, Fee Policy and Scholarship Policy (5.2.3), p. 11

text:

5.3.1 Scholarship for Outstanding performance in the fields of Sports/Culture/Fine
Arts/Sciences.
5.3.2 Scholarship for Differently-Abled.
5.3.3 The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are

5.4 Academic Performance Scholarship (During the Program)
To reward and motivate excellence in overall academic performance, scholarships are

a) All types of Scholarships shall be applicable only on the Tuition Fee for the

b) A student shall be eligible for only one scholarship in a given academic year.
c) All types of Scholarships shall be valid only for the concerned academic year.
d) Renewal of any type of scholarship is not automatic and shall be governed by the
terms and criteria as mentioned in this policy.
e) The number of Scholarships to be awarded under each type and sub -category for
the concerned academic year shall be solely decided by the Board of Management
on the recommendation of the University Scholarship Committee.
f) A student who has been selected for a scholarship shall provide a joint (with
parent) undertaking.
The scholarship shall be terminated and the scholarship amount shall be returned to the
University, in case of the following violations;
i) Any information provided in the scholarship application form is found to be
untrue or fraudulent;

Amended Academic Regulations approved in the 6th Meeting of the Academic Council held on July 29, 2025 vide Resolution No 6.16.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations, pp. 12-15

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 1. Academic Calendar]
1.1. The academic activities of the University are regulated by the Academic
Calendar approved by the Academic Council and notified by the
University at least one calendar month before the commencement of each
academic year.
1.2. An academic year in the University shall normally be divided into two
semesters consisting of ninety (90) University working days each, known
as ‘Odd Semester’ (normally from July / August to December) and ‘Even
Semester’ (normally from January to April/May).
1.3. An additional Academic Term known as the ‘Summer Term’ may be
scheduled during the summer break (June to July).
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 1. Academic Calendar, p. 15

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.1. Every student shall complete the mandatory requirement known as the
‘Registration’ procedure and register for the prescribed and approved
Courses to be pursued during a given Academic Term. This Registration
process is mandatory every Semester / Academic Term till the
completion of the Program. The University Registrar's Office manages the
registration process and related activities.
2.2. The prescribed date for Registration shall be announced in the Academic
Calendar and through notifications issued by the University to this
effect.
2.3. The Chairperson of the Program Academic Committee (PAC) of each
Program/School shall communicate the list of approved/prescribed
Courses available for Registration in the concerned Semester to the
University Registrar's Office for Notification as per the specified dates in
the Academic Calendar.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.1), p. 15

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.4. Every student after consulting their Faculty Advisor [Mentor] is required
to register for the approved Courses offered in the given Academic Term
at the commencement of each Semester/Academic Term on the days
fixed for such registration as notified in the Academic Calendar or the
University Notification to this effect.
On joining the University, each student is assigned a Faculty Advisor
[Mentor] to counsel the student on matters related to the Registration
process.
2.5.
Without registration, any academic activity (Course / Internship /
Project, etc.) undergone by a student will not be counted towards the
requirements for the award of the Degree. No student shall be permitted
to attend classes without completing the appropriate registration
procedure.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.4), pp. 15-16

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.6. Late registration shall only be permitted in case of medical exigencies,
specifically hospitalization, trauma or contagious disease s, for the
student / family member , and participation in approved
competitions/events as detailed in Sub-Clauses 2.6.1 and 2.6.2. below.
In such cases, a student may be permitted for late registration with prior
approval from the concerned Program Chair / Dean of the concerned
School. In the absence of Program Chair / Dean of the concerned School,
the authorised faculty shall approve.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.6), p. 16

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]

contagious disease only), for the student / family member, the
maximum period permissible for late registration shall not be more
than two (02) calendar weeks counted from the specified date of
Registration announced by the University. The student must
produce the medical certificates, medical prescriptions, hospital

officer of the hospital where the concerned student / family

not be eligible for late registration if they fail to produce authentic

section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.6.1), p. 16

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.6.2. If a student of second and subsequent semesters has been selected
/ permitted by the University to participate in State / National /
International Competitions / Events, the concerned student may
be permitted for late registration. The student must produce duly
attested documents and/or Certificates to be eligible for the
provision of late registration. The number of days for which the
concerned student shall be given permission for late registration
shall be approved by the Vice Chancellor on recommendation of
both the Director, Campus Life and Program Chair of the
concerned school.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.6.2), p. 16

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.7. In case of any other reason for late registration other than the cases
specified in Sub -Clauses 2.6.1 and 2.6.2 above, the maximum
permissible period for late registration shall not be more than one (01)
calendar week counted from the specified date of Registration announced
by the University.
Further, the student shall pay a Late Fee for late registration as specified
by the University at the commencement of the Academic Term. No
relaxation whatsoever shall be given on attendance requirement in case
of late registration. Under no circumstances shall such a student be
permitted to register for the Academic Term after the permissible period

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.9. Students are not permitted to re -register for Courses which they have
already passed, except under the provisions and conditions of Clauses
11.4.3 and 12.5.
2.10. A student shall be permitted to register in the next Semester only if all
the following conditions are fulfilled:
2.10.1. The student has paid all specified fees of the University as per the
University Fee Policy and payment schedule.
2.10.2. The student has cleared all University, Hostel, Transport and

2.10.3. The student has not been debarred from registering on any

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.12. A student who is eligible for registration, but fails to register for the
Academic Term within the specified dates, including the late registration
date, shall be removed from the rolls for the concerned Academic Term
and shall not be permitted to attend classes for the concerned Academic
Term. Such a student shall have to register for the corresponding
Academic Term in the next academic year.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.12), p. 17

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.13. Pre-Registration (Specialization / Minor / Open and other specified
Courses) for higher Semesters:
All students (other than the students admitted to the first Semester of a
Program) intending to register for the next higher Semester are required
to complete the Pre -Registration process. A student, after consultation
with the Faculty Advisor [Mentor], is required to declare their intent to
register for Specialization / Minor / Open and any other specified
Courses, as/if applicable, well in advance, before the actual start of the
concerned Academic Term, through the process of Pre -Registration as
per the schedule/dates announced in the Academic Calendar and/or the
notifications issued by the University to this effect. Specialization /
Minor courses will be offered only if a minimum of ten (10) students
register for the same. However, the program chair may permit to offer the
courses at their discretion.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.13), pp. 17-18

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.14. Course Pre-Requisites
For a student to register for some Courses, it may be required either to
have exposure in, or to have completed satisfactorily, or to have prior
earned credits in some specified Courses. Such Course pre -requisites
shall be specified in the concerned Program Regulations / Course Plan
as approved by the PAC.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.14), p. 18

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.15. Changes in Registration: Add/Drop
Students may add and drop Courses after consulting the concerned
Faculty Advisors [Mentor] and submit a request for add/drop to the
concerned Program Chair/Dean of Schools within two weeks of
commencement of classes for add/drop.
On approval, the Course(s) shall be added, and the dropped Course(s)
will not appear on the Grade Card (Refer Clause 8.14).
Student may seek transfer from one Program to another before the
commencement of registration for the Second Year with due approval of
both Program Chairs, subject to the eligibility criteria and provisions of
the academic regulations. On no account shall a transfer from one
Program to another be allowed beyond the stipulated period.
2.16. A student of a particular degree Program shall register for the
appropriate number of Course credits in each Semester/session that is
within the minimum and maximum limits specific to that degree Program
as stipulated in the Program Regulations.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.15), p. 18

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration]
2.17. Audit a Course
Auditing a Course is a provision for a student who may opt to register for
a Course to acquire knowledge / skills, but not to earn credits and grade
points.
A student who desires to register for auditing a Course shall consult their
Faculty Advisor [Mentor] and seek approval of the concerned Course
Instructor (Refer Clause 8.1). Registration shall only be permitted as per
the criteria and guidelines prescribed by the concerned Course
Instructor and duly approved by the concerned PAC. The student only
earns a “S” [satisfactory] OR “U” [unsatisfactory] for Audited Course.
Audited Courses shall not count towards completing the degree
requirements. In the event that the student secures a U grade in an audit
course, which is non mandatory , it will be deemed that such a student
has discontinued the course. The U grade will not be reflected in the
transcript.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 2. Registration (2.17), pp. 18-19

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 3. Academic Credits - Course Credit Structure]
The Credit Structure is used to define various types of Courses to provide for
the appropriate pedagogy and methods of assessment and evaluation. The
flexibility required to accomplish the Course learning objectives and outcomes
can be provided for, while retaining a common framework for Credit allocation.
More importantly, it is necessary to have a transparent, credible and robust
system for planning, delivery and evaluation of each Course of the diverse
Programs of study of the University.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 3. Academic Credits - Course Credit Structure, p. 19

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 3. Academic Credits - Course Credit Structure]
3.1. The Credit Structure for defining and categorizing Courses is the L – T –
P (Lecture – Tutorial – Practical) framework. The Course Credits are fixed
based on the following norms:
Lecture / Tutorial: One (01) contact/classroom hour per week is
assigned One (01) Credit.
Practical: Two (02) hours per week of practice/studio/laboratory/field
and other similar practice or skill development components, are assigned
One (01) Credit.
For example:
A Course with L – T – P structure of 4 – 0 – 0 will be assigned 4 Credits.
A Course with L – T – P structure of 3 – 1 – 0 will be assigned 4 Credits.
A Course with L – T – P structure of 0 – 0 – 4 will be assigned 2 Credits.
A Course with L – T – P structure of 1 – 0 – 4 will be assigned 3 Credits.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 3. Academic Credits - Course Credit Structure (3.1), p. 19

3.2. Practice/Skill based Courses like Industry Internship, Capstone,

L-T-P structure as defined in Clause 3.1, are assigned the number of

3.3. A student earns credits by satisfactorily completing Courses and other
academic activities every Academic Term. The credits associated with a
Course are dependent upon the number of hours of instruction per week
in that Course. Similarly, the credit associated with any of the other
learning activities is dependent upon the quantum of work expected to

The Program Regulations is a set of Program specific regulations, as applicable,
and the Program Curriculum for the concerned Degree Program. The Program
Regulations shall be recommended by the concerned Board of Studies for
approval of the Academic Council and shall include the following details:
4.1. Program specific regulations with respect to admission criteria, Program
duration, mandatory minimum credit requirements for the award of the
Degree, assessment and evaluation guidelines/criteria, and any other
regulations mandated by concerned Government Regulatory Bodies, where
applicable, for the specific Program of study.
The concerned Program Regulations shall provision, as applicable, for
various types and title / nomenclature of qualifications. as per the
guidelines outlined by the University Grants Commission (UGC). Further,
the Program Regulations shall specify the process of recommendation and
approval for the award of such qualifications.

[Section III - Academic Regulations > 4. Program Regulations]
4.2. The Program Structure and Curriculum with the list of Courses offered for

English shall be the medium of instruction and evaluation.
Any other language, if required for a specific Course (or Courses), shall be
proposed by concerned Board of Studies and approved by the Academic Council
and Board of Management of the University.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 5. Medium of Instruction and Evaluation, p. 20

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 6. Maximum Duration for the Completion of a Program]
6.1. The permissible maximum duration (number of academic years) for
completion of a Program (Undergraduate and Postgraduate) shall be (N+2)
years, where N is the normal duration (number of academic years) as
prescribed by the concerned Program Regulations.
6.2. The enrolment of the student who fails to complete the mandatory
requirements for the award of the concerned Degree (Refer to Section 15)
in the prescribed maximum duration, shall stand terminated and no
Degree shall be awarded.
6.3. The time taken by the student to improve Grades/CGPA, and in case of
temporary withdrawal/re-joining (Refer to Clause 13.1), shall be counted
in the permissible maximum duration for completion of a Program.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 6. Maximum Duration for the Completion of a Program, pp. 20-21

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements]
7.1. In order to maintain academic rigour and excellence, all students must
attend every lecture, tutorial, studio, field work, laboratory, practical
classes and all other such curricular sessions as prescribed by the Program
requirements.
7.2. To account for approved leave of absence to appear for end semester
examination, the attendance requirement shall be a minimum of seventy
five percent (75%) of the classes actually conducted in every Course the
student has registered for in the Academic Term.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements (7.1), p. 21

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements]
7.3. Further, if a student or their family member/s suffer serious medical
exigencies of hospitalization, trauma or contagious disease, the concerned
student may submit a leave request , together with documents to the
Faculty Advisor [Mentor] for recommendation to the Program Chair. The
student shall be given an additional relaxation in attendance in the
Course(s) where there is a shortage subject to the approval by the Vice -
Chancellor. However, on no account whatsoever, shall the minimum
requirement of attendance be less than sixty five percent (65% ) of the
classes actually conducted in every Course the student has registered for
in the Academic Term. The student shall not be eligible for this special
provision if they fail to produce authentic medical certificates and relevant
documents, including fitness certificate (in the case of student only), on the
day of rejoining the classes, in support of the medical exigency.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements (7.3), p. 21

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements]
7.4. If a student has been selected to represent the State and/or India in State
/ National / International Events / Competitions, the concerned student
may be given relaxation in attendance requirement (in the Course(s) where
there is a shortage) for the concerned period of absence recommended by
the Director, Campus Life and the Faculty Advisor [Mentor] to the Program
Chair and thereafter approval by the Vice Chancellor . However, on no
account whatsoever, shall the minimum requirement of attendance be less
than sixty five percent (65%) of the classes actually conducted in every
Course the student has registered for in the Academic Term. The student
shall not be eligible for this special provision if they fail to produce
authentic certificates of participation in the aforementioned Events /
Completions.

adhered to without exception. Such specific requirements, as applicable,
shall be prescribed in the Program Regulations of the concerned Program
of study.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements (7.5), p. 22

[Section III - Academic Regulations > 7. Attendance Requirements]
7.6. Shortage of Attendance:
A student with shortage of attendance (as specified in Clause 7.2 and the
applicable provisions of Clauses 7.3, 7.4 and 7.5) shall not be permitted to
appear for the End Term Examinations, as applicable, of the Course(s) in
which the attendance shortfall exists, irrespective of the student’s academic
performance in the final components of Continuous Assessments. The
student shall be declared as having failed to complete the Course due to
shortage of attendance and shall be given the ‘FA’ Grade (Refer to Sub -
Clause 8.13.3) in the concerned Course(s).
The student is cautioned that shortage of attendance may result in the loss
of an Academic Year. It is the sole responsibility of the student to ensure
that they do not fall under shortage of attendance.

[Section III - Academic Regulations > 8. Teaching, Evaluation and Grading System]
8.1. Courses from the approved Program Structure may be offered during any
Academic Term. Each approved Course, whenever offered in any given
Academic Term, shall be conducted by the assigned Course Instructor.
8.2. The Course Instructors and Tutors/Teaching Assistants, if any, for all the
Courses to be offered by the School/Department during any Academic
Term shall be assigned by the concerned Program Chair/Dean of School.
8.3. The Course Plan, prepared by the assigned Course Instructor, for every
Course that is offered in a given Academic Term shall be approved by the
concerned Program Chair and BoS.
8.4. The Course Instructor shall be responsible for conducting the Course,
conducting the assessments and examinations, evaluating the performance
of the students and awarding the grades at the end of the Academic Term.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 8. Teaching, Evaluation and Grading System (8.1), p. 22

8.5. The academic performance evaluation of a student in a Course shall be
according to the University Letter Grading System based on the class
performance distribution of the Course.
8.6. Academic performance evaluation of every registered student in every
Course registered is done through various components of Continuous
Assessments spread across the Semester and including the End Term
Examinations. The nature of components of Continuous Assessments and
the weightage given to each component of Continuous Assessments,
including the End Term Examinations, shall be prescribed in the Program
Regulations of the Program concerned.
8.7. Evaluation System: Components and Weightage
The University shall follow a Course Instructor led continuous evaluation
system. The components and recommended weightages of the evaluation
system are summarized in Table 1 below:

| Lecture-based Course | End Term Examination / Comprehensive | 30% (minimum) to 40% (maximum) |
| Practice-based Course (P in the L-T-P structure predominates, e.g. 0-0-4, 1-0-4, 1-0-2) | Continuous Assessments | 70% (minimum) to 100% (maximum) |
| Practice-based Course | End Term Examination / Jury / Project / Viva Voce | 30% (maximum) |

the approved Course Plan, and other announcements as required at the

text:
[Section III - Academic Regulations > 8. Teaching, Evaluation and Grading System]
8.9. Grading is the process of rewarding the students for their overall
performance in each Course. The University follows the system of Relative
Grading to classify the students based on their relative performance in the
concerned Course. Absolute Grading may be used in case the number of
students registered in the concerned Course is less than ten (10). The
Course Instructor shall declare the manner of grading in such instance.
Grading shall be done at the end of the Academic Term by considering the
aggregate performance of the student in all components of Continuous
Assessments prescribed for the Course. Letter Grades shall be awarded to
a student based on her/his overall performance relative to the class
performance distribution in the concerned Course. These letter grades not
only indicate a qualitative assessment of the student’s performance but
also carry a quantitative (numeric) equivalent called the Grade Point.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 8. Teaching, Evaluation and Grading System (8.9), p. 24

The University follows the system of Letter Grades with associated Grade
Points on a Scale of 10. The Letter Grades and Associated Grade Points
are summarized in Table 2:

8.11. Earned Credits
This refers to the credits assigned to the Courses in which a student has
obtained either ‘S’ grade (in other than Audit Courses), or any one of the
grades ‘O’, ‘A+’, ‘A’, ‘B+’, ‘B’, ‘C’, ‘D’ (but not ‘F’ or ‘FA’).8.12. Cut-off Marks for ‘O’ and ‘F’ Grades
The cut-off marks for ‘O’ grade and for ‘F’ grade (aggregate of the marks
assigned for components of Continuous Assessments, and the marks
assigned for the End Term Examination, as applicable), will be decided by
the Course Instructor based on the specific relevant details of the class
performance distribution (using appropriate class performance statistics
parameters). However, as a general guideline, the minimum cut -off marks
for ‘O’ and ‘F’ grade shall be 85% and 35% respectively. In exceptional
cases, w here the ‘O’ or ‘F’ grade is proposed below the aforementioned
minimum cut -off marks, the concerned Course Instructor shall provide
justification for the same to the concerned Program Chair, subject to the
approval by the Statutory Grading Approval Committee before the
respective grades are awarded.
The minimum/maximum cut -off marks for the intermediate grades are
determined by the Course Instructor using appropriate

class performance distribution.
8.13. Description of Grades:
8.13.1 ‘O’ Grade
An ‘O’ grade stands for outstanding achievement, relative to the
class, and the Course Instructor shall take utmost care in awarding
this highest grade.
8.13.2 ‘D’ Grade
The ‘D’ grade stands for marginal performance and is the minimum
passing grade.8.13.3 ‘F’ and ‘FA’ Grades
a) The ‘F’ grade denotes very poor performance, i.e., failure in a Course
due to poor performance and the Course Instructor shall take utmost
care while awarding this lowest grade.
Further, ‘F’ grade shall be given to a student who is Absent for the
End Term Examination as specified for a concerned Course. If the
absence is solely due to medical exigencies specifically
hospitalization, trauma or contagious disease only, the placeholder
Grade ‘I’ will be given (Refer Sub Clause 8.13.5).
b) ‘FA’ grade denotes poor attendance i.e., failure in a Course due to
attendance shortage (Refer Clause 7.6).
c) The students who have received ‘F’ grade in a Course in the
immediate subsequent semester may be allowed to appear for a
Make-Up Examination. The Make -Up Examinations will be
conducted possibly along with that arranged for those students
who received the ‘I’ grade, within the period announced in the
Academic Calendar.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 8. Teaching, Evaluation and Grading System (8.13), pp. 25-26

d) Only regular registrants of a given Course during a given Academic
Semester who have obtained ‘F’ or ‘I’ grade in the Course will be
permitted to appear for the Make-up Examination.
e) Students who continue to have ‘F’ grade after the Make -Up
Examination are required to re-register for the Course whenever it
is offered subsequently.
f) All the ‘F’ and ‘FA’ grades secured in any Course shall be recorded
on the grade card.
g) A student who obtains ‘FA’ grade in any Course shall re-register for
the Course in the subsequent Academic Term whenever the Course
is offered until a passing grade is obtained. However, for a course
that is not mandatory in which ‘FA’ grade has been obtained, the
student may either repeat the same Course or register for any other

permitted to opt for change of Minor only once till completion of the
program.8.13.4 ‘S’ and ‘U’ Grades
a) Grades ‘S’ and ‘U’ do not have any associated grade points and
are recommended for use in the evaluation of select Non -Taught
Credit Courses [ Summer Internship ], as applicable, and for
grading Audit Courses.
b) The ‘S’ grade denotes satisfactory performance and completion of
a Course. The associated credits are earned and counted for the
mandatory credits requirements as specified in the concerned

c) The ‘U’ grade denotes unsatisfactory performance and non -
completion of a Course. The student shall have to re -register for

awarded. This clause is also applicable to Audit Courses.
d) In the event that the student secures a U grade in an audit course,
which is non mandatory it will be deemed that such a student has
discontinued the course. The U grade will not be reflected in the
transcript.
e) The ‘S’ or ‘U’ grade secured in a Course shall be recorded on the

Grade Card.8.13.5 ‘I’ Grade
‘I’ is a placeholder grade which denotes “incomplete” performance in
any Course or Courses, due to one of the following conditions:
a) Absence at the End Term Examination solely due to medical
exigencies, specifically hospitalization, trauma or contagious
disease. The ‘I’ grade shall be replaced by an appropriate letter
grade after the student clears the Make -Up Examination (Refer
Clause 9.4).
b) In case of a reported case of unfair means (plagiarism,
malpractice, etc.) under investigation against a student in the End
Term Examination or any component of assessment of any
Course(s), the student will be given an I Grade . The placeholder
grade ‘I’ shall be replaced with a regular grade based on
recommendations of the panel constituted to investigate the case,
and the subsequent approval of the Registrar. Students will not
be eligible for the Make-up examination if the investigating panel
recommends a ‘F’ grade.
section: Section III - Academic Regulations > 8. Teaching, Evaluation and Grading System, p. 27

The Course(s) in which a student has received ‘I’ grade shall not
be included in the SGPA/CGPA calculations (Refer Clause 8.15).
8.14. Grade Card:
A Grade Card for an Academic Term is the record of the student’s
performance in the Courses the student has registered for in that Academic
Term of the Program of study.
The Grade Card shall contain the following details pertaining to the
student’s academic performance:
a) The List of Courses (which includes Course Name, Course Code and
associated Credits) registered for by the student in the concerned
Academic Term [ Semester], Make -Up Examinations and Summer
Term as applicable;
b) The Grade obtained in each of the concerned Courses; and,
c) The SGPA and CGPA obtained by the student.
d) Transcript will be issued on completion of the Program.8.15 Transcript:
A University Transcript is an official academic document that comprehensively
records a student's academic progress throughout their time at the university.
It also serves as a formal reference for determining eligibility to receive the degree
certificate during convocation. The transcript provides detailed information on
every course a student has registered for and successfully completed, including
the Course Code, Course Title, Grade Obtained, Credit, Semester of
Completion, and Course Bucket (e.g., University Core, Program Foundation,
etc.).
The Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is computed based solely on
courses that carry grade points. However, the following rules apply:
x Mandatory courses graded as S (Satisfactory) or U (Unsatisfactory) are
listed in the transcript but are excluded from CGPA calculation, as they do
not carry grade points.
x Audit courses are included only if the student earns an 'S' grade. If a 'U'

recorded.

transcript.

grade points secured in all the Courses registered for by the student during
that Semester. SGPA for a particular Semester (and Summer Term, as
applicable) is computed as follows:

Presentations, Take Home Assignments, Group Discussions etc., which
are spread across the Semester. The nature of components of Continuous
Assessments and the weightage given to each component shall be
mentioned in the respective Course Plan. In case a student misses any
component of the continuous assessment, except the final continuous
assessment, it is up to the discretion of the course instructor to offer an
extended deadline or alternative assignment, but before the academic
term ends. Final component of Continuous assessment shall be
conducted after ascertaining the attendance requirement.

indicated in the Academic Calendar, shall be prepared by the Registrar
(Evaluation) in consultation with the Program Chairs/Deans of Schools
and shall be announced with due approval of the Vice Chancellor, at least
one (01) calendar month before the commencement of the End Term
Examinations.
9.3. The detailed schedule of the Make -Up Examinations, where applicable,
shall be published by Registrar (Evaluation) in consultation with the
Program Chairs/Deans of Schools and shall be announced with due
approval of the Vice Chancellor, at least two (02) calendar weeks before
the commencement of the Make-Up Examinations.

University Examinations shall be notified by the Registrar (Evaluation)

[Section III - Academic Regulations > 9. Examinations]
9.5. Make-Up Examinations
Make-Up Examinations are a provision for a student to complete a Course
(or Courses) in which she/he received an ‘F’ grade or was given the
placeholder grade ‘I’ to reappear in the End Term Examination component
of a Course (or Courses), subject to the conditions mentioned below in
Sub-Clauses 9.5.1 and 9.5.2. Students may also avail the benefit of Make-
up examination to improve her/his CGPA. In no other circumstances shall
Make-Up Examinations be available to students.9.5.1 A student who fails to appear for the End Term Examinations
in some or all Courses due to medical exigencies, specifically
hospitalization, trauma or contagious disease and the said student
informs the Program Chair/Dean concerned in a timely manner (i.e.,
on or before thecommencement of the said End Term Examinations),
may submit a request to the Registrar [Evaluation] of the University
within the duly notified dates, along with the prescribed fee for the
Make-Up Examinations fixed by the University from time to time. On
the basis of the student’s performance in the Make-Up Examinations
and considering the marks obtained by the student in all other
Continuous Assessments, as applicable, the final letter grade
awarded shall replace the placeholder grade ‘I’.
In case, the application of the student for Make -Up Examinations is
rejected by the Registrar [Evaluation], the student shall be declared

“Failed” in the concerned Course(s) and the placeholder grade ‘I’ shall
be replaced with ‘F’ grade in the concerned Course(s). Further, the
student shall have to complete the Course(s) as per the provisions
and conditions prescribed in Clause 11 and Sub-Clause 11.4.2.
Further, if the concerned student does not avail the Make -Up
Examinations, or is absent for the Make -Up Examinations, the
student shall be declared “Failed” in the concerned Course(s) and the
placeholder grade ‘I’ shall be replaced with ‘F’ grade. Further, the
student shall have to complete the Course(s) as per the provisions
and conditions prescribed in Clause 11 and Sub-Clause 11.4.2.

[Section III - Academic Regulations > 10. Academic Appeals]
10.1. The University is committed to keep the entire process of evaluation
transparent. Within three (03) working days of announcement of results,
if a student needs clarification on the marks / grade obtained, the Course
instructor shall explain to a student why they received the grade awarded.
A mechanism for review of grades is incorporated in the evaluation
system.

[Section IV - Code of Conduct]
Code of Conduct
1. Introduction
The Vidyashilp University Student Code of Conduct is a set of standards of conduct
expected of students during their tenure as students of the University.
The aim of the University is to sculpt ‘ vidya’ (education) and not the student. In
Sanskrit, it is said that ‘ vidya dadati vinayam ’, meaning, that education imparts
character. The aim, therefore, is reflective of the need for students to learn values such
as respect for fellow beings as well as display civility and inclusiveness in their
behavior towards other students, faculty, research scholars and support staff.
At VU, the various Schools function with an interdisciplinary interdependence.
Diversity in thinking and using a pluralistic approach to learning is something that is
replete in the University system. A VU graduate must inculcate a sense of reverence
for the knowledge derived from other domains.
The VU curriculum is structured such that, along with domain knowledge the
section: Section IV - Code of Conduct, p. 43

text:
[Section IV - Code of Conduct]
students must learn aspects of citizenship, sportsmanship and concern for the
environment.
2. Unique “VU Experience”
The essence of Vidyashilp University is to create a unique “VU Experience” – an
enjoyable journey of learning from one another and learning together through
intentional collaboration between individuals and groups from diverse cultures and
backgrounds.
VU’s purpose is to create a diverse, inclusive community and environment where
faculty, staff, students and parents, and alumni feel connected to one another by a
common sense of purpose and develop a distinctive ability to lead and serve in diverse
contexts.
The “VU Experience” is a collective endeavour to inculcate the “Vidyashilp Graduate
Attributes”.
3. Attributes of a Vidyashilp Graduate
(What VU endeavors its students and alumni to BE!)
The unique “VU Experience” is a journey with an aspiration that each and every
student of Vidyashilp will grow towards conscientious citizenship and exemplify the
section: Section IV - Code of Conduct, pp. 43-44

text:
[Section IV - Code of Conduct]
attributes of being:
3.1 Self-Aware: The student sojourn is an experience of self -discovery and self -
knowledge. Explore one’s intellectual curiosity and humanity;
3.2 Confident: The self-awareness to manifest a developed sense of self -purpose
and confidence to pursue one’s goals;
3.3 Empathetic: Being able to respect and appreciate other people; cataly ze the
free exchange of ideas in an interdependent, diverse community and explore
ways to serve in harmony;
3.4 Resourceful: Take responsibility to apply knowledge, scholarship and creative
practice to benefit society and the growth of the nation, and as a3.5 Leader: Serve society with a commitment to the underprivileged and deprived
in the community.
4. VU Student Code of Conduct
The Code applies to the conduct of students on campus. It also applies to their
conduct off -campus and on social media, if the same is likely to have serious
consequences or adverse impact on the University's interests or reputation. Further,
it applies to conduct when students participate in the University’s programs or
activities or such activities where the student represents the University or is deemed
to be an ambassador of the University. The conduct applies to students living in
residences arranged by the University too.
The Code of Conduct has been established to communicate the expectations of proper
and professional conduct in line with the values and standards upheld by the founders
of the University. It serves as the basis, on which, students should make decisions
section: Section IV - Code of Conduct (3.1), p. 44

text:
[Section IV - Code of Conduct]
related to the best interests of themselves, the faculty and other staff in the University,
rather than a statement of what to do or should not do while at the University.
4.1 Students are expected to maintain the highest standards of discipline and
dignified behavior inside as well as outside the University campus. They shall
abide by the rules and regulations of the University and should act in a way that
highlights the discipline and esteem of the University.
4.2 Students are expected to maintain integrity and honesty in all their actions;
whether in class during lectures, tutorials or practical sessions; while appearing
for any form of evaluation or any other co -curricular or extra -curricular
activities.
4.3 Students are expected to be trustworthy in their actions when given any
responsibility during the conduct of co-curricular or extra-curricular activity by
the faculty o r other university staff, by acting in a reliable and dependable
manner.

[Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines]
Guidelines on Banning Ragging and Anti Ragging Measures
1. Introduction
Pursuant to the directives of the Honourable Supreme Court of India and in
accordance with the UGC Regulations, on curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher
Educational Institutions, 2009, the University is committed to ensuring no ragging
takes place by instituting stringent anti -ragging measures and provisions for strict
punishments to defaulters. Ragging is a cognizable offence and Vidyashilp University
will take strict action against offenders.
2. Definition of Ragging
The University considers the definition of ragging as per UGC’s “Curbing the menace
of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions (third amendment), Regulations, 2016”
which states that:
" Any act of physical or mental abuse (including bullying and exclusion) targeted at
another student (fresher or otherwise) on the ground of color, race, religion, caste,
ethnicity, gender (including transgender), sexual orientation, appearance,
section: Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines, p. 49

text:
[Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines]
nationality, regional origins, linguistic identity, place of birth, place of residence or
economic background.”
The University educates the students enrolled in various programs at the beginning
of each academic year about the Anti -Ragging Policy and zero tolerance for ragging
at the University.
Each student, as well as his/her parents/ guardian, are mandatorily required to
submit separate undertakings in the form of an affidavit at the time of admission to
the effect that they are aware of the prohibition of ragging and the punishment
prescribed both under penal laws as well as under these regulations.
Anti-ragging hoardings, banners, and billboards are displayed at prominent places
on the University campus, including hostels, canteens, messes, cafeterias, buses,
playgrounds, lawns, labs, etc.
Surprise checks of hostels/canteens/cafeterias/bus stops are carried out regularly.
A close and regular liaison is maintained with the local police to guard against the
section: Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines, pp. 49-50

text:
[Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines]
incident of ragging. FIR will be lodged in the police station on all reported ragging
cases.
Daily briefing of freshers is carried out by counsellors and coordinators. An anti -
ragging committee of the students is also formed.
In case any student encounters ragging by any of the senior students, he/she is
immediately required to contact the members of the anti-ragging committee, who will
take immediate corrective action and necessary proceedings will be initiated against
the culprits engaged in ragging activities.
3. Prohibition of Ragging
3.1 Ragging within the University Campus including its Institutions /
Departments and Hostels is strictly prohibited.
3.2 Ragging in any form is prohibited also in the private lodges/buildings where
these University students are staying.
3.3 Ragging in any form is prohibited in Hostel, Mess, Canteen, Cafeteria &
Transport (University & Private).
section: Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines (3.1), p. 50

text:
[Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines]
3.4 No person including students/staff/faculty shall participate or abet or
propagate ragging in any form
4. Punishment for Ragging
4.1 Lodging FIR against the offender.
4.2 Rigorous Imprisonment for up to 3 years (under the court of law).
4.3 Fine up to Rs. 2, 50,000/-.
4.4 Expulsion from Vidyashilp University and consequent debarring from
admission to any other institution.
5. General Instructions
section: Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines (3.4), p. 50

text:
[Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines]
5.1 Anti-Ragging Committees
a) University shall form an “Anti -Ragging Committee” headed by the
Chairperson, appointed by the Vice Chancellor. It will comprise selected
faculty members, parents, students from the fresher’s category as well as
seniors and selected non-teaching staff.
b) This Committee will be fully and totally responsible to ensure that no
incidence of ragging as given in this regulation takes place and will also
monitor and ensure that the instructions of this regulation are followed
fully at all times.
c) The Committee will also maintain alert vigil at all times and ensure that
the Anti -Ragging Squads of the Institution carry out their functions
properly.5.2 Anti-Ragging Squads
a) The Chairperson of Anti Ragging Committee will constitute a number of
Anti-Ragging Squads. The number of squads will be based on the number
of blocks/floors and the strength of the students so that the Anti-Ragging
Measures can be effectively implemented.
b) Anti-Ragging Squads will comprise of senior faculty members and
responsible representatives of senior students and freshers. Its function
will include going around / patrolling the Department and the Campus
common areas, maintaining vigil at all times on all days by rotation as
decided by Director/Deputy Director/Programme Coordinator and taking
action if they notice any incidence of ragging either in their Department,
any other Department or on the Campus.
c) The Squads will also have the responsibility to investigate incidences of
ragging and to report to the Anti -Ragging Committee for immediate
action/punishment wherever required.
d) Director/Deputy Director/Programme Coordinator will forward the
section: Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines (5.1), pp. 50-51

text:
[Section V - Anti-Ragging Guidelines]
names of Anti -Ragging Committees and Anti -Ragging Squads to the
University Anti-Ragging Monitoring Cell.
e) On the report of the Anti -ragging Squad or any other person who
witnesses the incidence of ragging or on the complaint of any fresher
student, immediate action will be taken by the Anti -Ragging Committee
to decide appropriate punishment from the list of punishments in the
Regulation and award it with intimation to the University Administration.
6. Action Procedure
6.1 Anti-Ragging Squads will immediately report any incidence of ragging or
abetment of ragging noticed by them to the Anti -Ragging Committee of each
Department.
6.2 Faculty in charge of the Anti -Ragging Committee will take immediate action
as per the situation which may include:
a) Immediate suspension of involved students
b) Sending reinforcements or any medical help if required.
c) Forward the main gist/report of the incident to the Anti -Ragging
Committee.6.3 The Anti-Ragging Committee of the concerned Department will examine the
report and recommend appropriate punishment with intimation to the
University Administration.
7. Anti-Ragging affidavit
To ensure a safe and conducive learning environment for all students at Vidyashilp
University, it is mandatory for every student to fill the Anti-Ragging affidavit.
Steps to fill the Anti Ragging Affidavit in UGC
7. 1: Visit the website: https://www.antiragging.in/

Guidelines on Prevention of Sexual Harassment
1. Introduction
The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal)
Act, 2013 ("POSH Act") was enacted as a comprehensive legislation to provide a safe, secure
and enabling environment, free from sexual harassment to every woman. This statute was
enacted to fill the legislative void which had been partially addressed by the judiciary in
Vishaka and Others v. State of Rajasthan and Others (1997 (7) SCC 323). In this seminal
public interest litigation verdict, the Supreme Court of India had framed a set of guidelines
("Vishaka Guidelines") for dealing with instances of sexual harassment at the workplace,
which has now been codified in the POSH Act.
The Supreme Court of India held that sexual harassment of women is a violation of the
fundamental right of women to work in a safe environment.
The Supreme Court has defined ‘sexual harassment’ to include:
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, p. 57

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
1.1 "An unwanted conduct with sexual undertones if it occurs or which is persistent and
which demeans, humiliates or creates a hostile and intimidating environment or is
calculated to induce submission by actual or threatened adverse consequences and
includes any one or more or all of the following unwelcome acts or behavior (whether
directly or by implication), namely; -
a) any unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature;
b) demand or request for sexual favours;
c) making sexually colored remarks
d) physical contact and advances; or
e) showing pornography1.2 any one (or more than one or all) of the following circumstances, if it occurs or is
present in relation or connected with any behavior that has explicit or implicit sexual
undertones-
a) implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment as quid pro quo for sexual
favors;
b) implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in the conduct of work;
c) implied or explicit threat about the present or future status of the person
concerned;
d) creating an intimidating offensive or hostile learning environment;
e) humiliating treatment likely to affect the health, safety dignity or physical
integrity of the person concerned;
As a follow-up to the POSH Act, the University Grants Commission (UGC) – the apex
body for all higher education institutions - has come up with a regulation titled
University Grants Commission (Prevention, prohibition and redressal of sexual
harassment of women employees and students in higher educational institutions)
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment (1.1), pp. 57-58

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
Regulations, 2015. These regulations apply to all higher education institutions in
India. The provisions of the regulation are being adhered to by Vidyashilp University.
2. Responsibility of the University
VU commits to a zero -tolerance policy against sexual harassment. The management
reinforces that it will create a campus free from discrimination, harassment, retaliation or
sexual assault at all levels. VU will ensure compliance with all provisions of the regulation
and make the following efforts toward the same:
a) Constitute an Internal Complaints Committee to proactively curb all forms of
harassment of employees and students.
b) Publicly notify the provisions against sexual harassment and ensure their wide
dissemination in the prospectus, notice boards as well as the website, the penalty and
consequences of sexual harassment.
c) Organise training programmes/ workshops for the officers, functionaries , faculty and
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, p. 58

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
students, as indicated in the SAKSHAM Report (Measures for Ensuring the Safety of
Women and Programmes for Gender Sensitization on Campuses) of the UGC, to
sensitize them and ensure knowledge and awareness of the rights, entitlements and
responsibilities enshrined in the Act and under these regulations. These include
sessions to create awareness about what constitutes sexual harassment including
hostile environment harassment and quid pro quo harassment
d) Act decisively against all gender -based violence perpetrated against employees and
students of all sexes.
e) Bring to book those guilty of sexual harassment against its employees and students.
f) Monitor the timely submission of reports by the ICC as well as prepare an annual status
report with details on the number of cases filed and their disposal and submit the same
to the Commission.
3. Constitution of ICC
VU has established an Internal Complaints Committee to prevent, prohibit and redress and
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, p. 58

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
issues of sexual harassment. The ICC constitutes a lady presiding officer who is a senior
teaching faculty member, 2 other teaching faculty members, 2 members from th e non-
teaching, 3 students and an external member who works for an association that is
committed to the cause of women.
4. Role of ICC
a) provide assistance if an employee or a student chooses to file a complaint with the
police;
b) provide mechanisms or dispute redressal and dialogue to address issues through a
just and fair conciliation without undermining the complainant's rights, and minimize
the need for purely punitive approaches that lead to further resentment, alienation or
violence ;
c) protect the safety of the complainant by not divulging the person's identity, and provide
the mandatory relief by way of sanctioned leave or relaxation or attendance requirement
or transfer to another department or supervisor as required during the pendency of the
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, pp. 58-59

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
complaint, or also provide for the transfer of the offender;
d) ensure that victims or witnesses are not victimized or discriminated against while
dealing with complaints of sexual harassment; and
e) ensure the prohibition of retaliation or adverse action against a covered individual
because the employee or the student is engaged in protected activity.
5. How to lodge a complaint?
An aggrieved person is required to submit a written complaint to the ICC within three
months from the date of the incident and in case of a series of incidents within a period of
three months from the date of the last incident.
The Presiding Officer or any Member of the ICC shall render all reasonable assistance to
the person for making the complaint in writing.
6. Process and timeline of conducting an inquiry
a) The ICC shall, upon receipt of the complaint, send one copy of the complaint to the
respondent within a period of seven days of such receipt.
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, p. 59

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
b) Upon receipt of the copy of the complaint, the respondent shall file his or her reply to
the complaint along with the list of documents, and names and addresses of witnesses
within a period of ten days.
c) The inquiry has to be completed within a period of ninety days from the receipt of the
complaint. The inquiry report, with recommendations, if any, has to be submitted
within ten days from the completion of the inquiry to the Vice Chancellor of VU. Copy
of the findings or recommendations shall also be served on both parties to the
complaint.
d) The Vice Chancellor shall act on the recommendations of the committee within a period
of thirty days from the receipt of the inquiry report unless an appeal against the findings
is filed within that time by either party.
e) An appeal against the findings or /recommendations of the ICC may be filed by either
party before the Vice Chancellor within a period of thirty days from the date of the
recommendations.
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, pp. 59-60

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
f) The aggrieved party may seek conciliation in order to settle the matter. No monetary
settlement should be made as a basis of conciliation. The conciliation process shall be
facilitated through the ICC
g) The identities of the aggrieved party or victim or the witness or the offender shall not be
made public or kept in the public domain, especially during the process of the inquiry.
7. Action against offenders
a) Anyone found guilty of sexual harassment shall be punished in accordance with the
service rules of VU if the offender is an employee.
b) Where the respondent is a student, depending upon the severity of the offence VU may
i) withhold privileges of the student such as access to the library, auditoria, halls of
residence, transportation, scholarships, allowances, and identity card;
ii) suspend or restrict entry into the campus for a specific period;
iii) expel and strike off the name from the rolls of VU, including denial of readmission,
if the offence so warrants;
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, p. 60

text:
[Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment]
iv) award reformative punishments like mandatory counselling and, or, the
performance of community services.
8. Action Against False or frivolous Complaints
To ensure that the provisions for the protection of employees and students from sexual
harassment do not get misused, provisions against false or malicious complaints have to be
made. If the ICC concludes that the allegations made were false, malicious or the complaint
was made knowing it to be untrue, or forged or misleading information has been provided
during the inquiry, the complainant shall be liable to be punished.
section: Section VI - Prevention of Sexual Harassment, p. 60

[Section XI - Sports Policy]
Sports policy is crucial for fostering physical health, social cohesion, and economic growth
within a society. By promoting regular physical activity, it helps combat lifestyle -related
diseases and enhances mental well -being. It encourages inclusivity and social integration,
ensuring equal access to sports for all, while instilling values like teamwork and discipline
among youth. Economically, sports policy generates jobs, boosts local economies through
sports tourism, and stimulates infrastructure investment.
It also enhances national pride by supporting elite athletes and fostering success on the
international stage. Ensuring fairness and safety in sports, it promotes lifelong participation,
contributing to overall life quality and community well-being.
1. Objectives:
භ Enhance Physical Health: One of the main goals is to encourage everyone in the
university community to engage in regular physical activity. By doing so, we aim to
section: Section XI - Sports Policy, p. 79

text:
[Section XI - Sports Policy]
improve the overall health and well -being of all students, faculty, and staff. Regular
exercise can lead to better physical fitness, increased energy levels, and improved
mental health.
භ Boost Participation: Another important objective is to increase the number of people
participating in sports and recreational activities. We want to create more opportunities
for everyone to get involved, whether they are beginners or experienced athletes. By
boosting participation, we hope to create a more active and engaged university
community.
භ Skill Development: We aim to provide various opportunities for students to develop and
refine their sports skills. This includes offering training programs, workshops, and
coaching sessions. By helping students improve their abilities, we support their
personal growth and enhance their enjoyment of sports and physical activities.
භ Promote Team Spirit: Fostering a sense of teamwork, fair play, and sportsmanship is a
section: Section XI - Sports Policy, p. 79

text:
[Section XI - Sports Policy]
key focus. We want to create an environment where everyone values cooperation and
respect. Through team sports and group activities, participants can learn the
importance of working together, supporting each other, and competing with integrity.
භ Support Elite Athletes: For those students who excel in their sports, we are committed
to providing the necessary resources and support to help them achieve their best. This
includes access to high -quality training facilities, professional coaching, and ot her
resources that can aid in their athletic development. By supporting elite athletes, we
help them reach their full potential and represent the university with pride.
2. Scope
This policy is comprehensive and applies to every individual who is part of the Vidyashilp
University community, which includes students, faculty, and staff members. It encompasses
all sports and recreational activities that are organized, sponsored, or endorsed by the
section: Section XI - Sports Policy, p. 79

text:
[Section XI - Sports Policy]
university. This broad scope includes a variety of activities, ranging from intramural
competitions, where members of the university compete against each other, to intercollegiate
contests, which involve competition with other educational institutions. Additionally, the
policy covers fitness programs designed to promote health and well-being among participants,
as well as informal recreational activities that may not be part of a structured program but

[1. Course Registration]
Eligibility Criteria
Students with pending fees or incomplete documentation
are not eligible for course registration, and attendance will
not be recorded until the registration is fully completed.
• Course Registration on Digii
Course registration will be available on the Digii portal for
eligible students only. Students must select their courses,
verify credits, and submit the registration form online. Students
will not be allowed to attend classes without completing the
course registration.
• Faculty Advisor [Mentor]
Students are advised to consult their Faculty Advisor [Mentor]
to understand and seek clarity on selection of course(s), credits,
etc., prior to course registration.
• Registration Card Submission
After online registration, students must collect the hard copy of
the Registration Card from the Concern Department , get it
signed by the Faculty Advisor [Mentor] and Program Chair ,
and return the signed copy to the Course Registration Card to the
concern department.
section: 1. Course Registration

• Cohort & Attendance Details
Students can check their cohort details on the Digii portal after
course registration.
Daily attendance status for each course will also be available
on Digii. No attendance will be granted for any missed classes
due to late registration.
• Course Registration Deadline
The maximum permissible period for late registration shall not
be more than one (01) calendar week counted from the specified
date of Registration announced by the University. No extensions
will be granted.
• Late Registration
No late registration shall be permitted. However, considering
medical exigencies, specifically hospitalization, trauma or
contagious disease only, and participation in any
competitions/events a student may be permitted for late
registration with prior approval from the concerned Program
Chair/Dean of concerned School. The maximum period
permissible for late registration due to medical shall not be more

[10. General Guidelines]
To ensure a seamless university experience, all students are required to
adhere to the following guidelines:
• Students must wear the ID Card compulsory at all times while on
campus.
• Safety of equipment in the classroom : Utilize upgraded
classroom / lab facilities such as Interactive Display Panels (IDP),
chairs, and tables responsibly. Damages caused by intentional or
negligent behaviour will have consequences.
• Exercise mindfulness during meals : Eat in designated spaces,
especially in the cafeteria. Avoid eating in classrooms / Lab to
maintain a conducive learning environment.
• Use of internet services : University wi -fi is exclusively for
academic use. Using wi -fi other than academic purpose and video
streaming are prohibited. Violations will be viewed seriously.
• Maintain campus cleanliness : Do not litter. CCTV cameras
monitor for compliance and violations will result in consequences.
• Respect shared spaces : Sofas at reception are for guests. Use
section: 10. General Guidelines, p. 5

text:
[10. General Guidelines]
alternative seating in the lawn or cafeteria.
• Infirmary usage: Visit the infirmary if you are unwell.
•
section: 10. General Guidelines, p. 5

text:
[11. Vehicle and Parking Guidelines]
Vehicle access limitations: Vehicles are strictly not permitted to
drive beyond the designated parking point. Exceptions are made
only for emergencies (medical issues or disability).
• Speed limit enforcement : Vehicle speed within the campus is
limited to 20 kmph to ensure safety for all.
• Triple riding prohibition: Triple riding on two-wheelers is
strictly not allowed.
• Wearing a helmet is mandatory for two-wheeler riders.
• Reception access: Only vehicles driven by parents / guardians or
authorized drivers may drive till the reception.
• Carpool/bike pool protocol: Vehicles used for student carpooling
or bike pooling must stop at the parking point. Students must walk
from there; vehicles are not permitted to drop off students at
Reception and then park.
• Parking restrictions: Vehicles are not allowed to park at Reception
or in front of the Design Studio. Parking is permitted only in the
designated parking areas.

- Handbook clause 1.2: the Odd Semester normally runs July/August to December; the Even Semester runs January to April/May.
- Therefore the current term (September 2026) is the ODD semester of academic year 2026-27, and the NEXT semester is the EVEN semester (January-May 2027).
- A summer term (June-July 2027) may be offered, but which courses run in it is not specified (handbook 11.4, 11.5.5).
section: How the current semester is determined

text:
[Offering rule of thumb]
Courses in the semester spread are placed in a specific semester. Odd-semester courses (S1, S3, S5, S7) run in the odd term and even-semester courses (S2, S4, S6, S8) run in the even term. A course placed in an even semester is therefore not offered in the current (odd) term. Offerings of specialization/minor courses also require at least 10 registered students unless the Program Chair permits otherwise (handbook 2.13).

Happy to welcome you to the School of Business and Entrepreneurship at Vidyashilp University.

- Objectives:
  - Stabilize inflation
  - Promote employment
  - Support economic growth
- "For-India-Target: It India's primary fiscal policy instrument.
- Revenue/Levy: Tax-based spending, or tax-cuts + investment and demand. Contractionary: Proposed spending or higher taxes + Controls inflation.

text:
[B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 2. Economic Outcomes]
- AD (nominal GDP) (Y) (Y= C+I+G+(X-M) indicated by the equation: AD = C+I+G+(X-M)
- Increased spending raises AD and GDP, but may also cause inflation.
- Inflation can result from a decreased spending. But taxation helps curb accelerated-driven price rises.
- Employment policies like MGNREGA show how fiscal intervention reduces rural unemployment.
- Fiscal policy also impacts macro and housing markets, influencing investor confidence.
source_file: Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) in Economics Brochure.pdf
section: B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 2. Economic Outcomes, p. 9

text:
[B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 3. Keynesian vs. Classical Perspectives]
- Classical economists believe in minimal government intervention, arguing that free markets self-correct, distribute balanced budgets and private sector-led growth.
- Keynesian economics advocate for active fiscal intervention during downturns, using government spending to boost demand and reduce unemployment.
- India's approach blends both theories ->
- Classical policies: 1991, LPG reforms, FDI, privatization.
- Keynesian policies: 2008 crisis stimulus, COVID-19 relief measures.
- Multi-modal shifts (in-between): the two extremes during crises and fiscal restraint during stability.
source_file: Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) in Economics Brochure.pdf
section: B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 3. Keynesian vs. Classical Perspectives, p. 9

text:
[B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 4. Statistical Analysis of Indicator Trends]
- Government Spending Increased post-COVID; for welfare and infrastructure but slower in 2024-25 due to fiscal consolidation.
- GDP Growth: Strong recovery after COVID-19, driven by investment and demand.
- Tax Revenues: Fell during the pandemic. But recovered due to increased collection and rising consumption.
- Inflation: High post-COVID rose with government stimulus but moderated with tax adjustments.
- Unemployment: Dropped during lockdowns. Improved with fiscal weapons, but rose again in 2023-24 due to global and technological shifts.
source_file: Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) in Economics Brochure.pdf
section: B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 4. Statistical Analysis of Indicator Trends, p. 9

text:
[B.A. (Hons.) Economics: ROLE OF FISCAL POLICY IN THE INDIAN ECONOMY > 5. COVID-19 Fiscal Policy]
- India's fiscal reaction gradually evolved, from a 1% direct resistance (cash transfers, food subsidies) and progressive to investment-led recovery (PLI schemes, capital expenditure).
- The ₹20 lakh crore Atmanirbhar Bharat package offered liquidity and credit guarantees, but was criticized for lacking direct fiscal stimulus.
- The fiscal deficit peaked at 9.2% of GDP in 2021, but recovery was aided by higher tax receipts and industrial expansion.
- Debate Concerns about the rising public debt, the policy stretch in consensus between short-term market and long-term economic stability.
source_file: Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) in Economics Brochure.pdf
